correctness.rationale: For each unordered two-symbol pair, the Type-A first/last differing interval is intrinsic and unique (Cai–Kiah–Nguyen–Yaakobi, Proposition 9). Both possible alternating phases are run-limited iff the left and right context boundary runs, when using a selected central symbol, are shorter than r. The exact admissible context series is (1+S_r-2z^r)/(1-(q-1)S_r); the unrestricted length>=2 alternating interval contributes u^2z^2/(1-uz). Formal multiplication gives the all-q, all-r>=2 bivariate edge count without double counting. For r>=2 the denominator has a unique simple strictly dominant root in (0,1), so coefficient extraction proves the edge-conditioned geometric span limit and the average-degree slope. A direct independent deletion-deck enumerator and an exact rational-recurrence/terminal-run dynamic program passed finite tests; no finite check is treated as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The all-q unrestricted edge result already counts arbitrary outside contexts and the special zero-repeat case r=1 is already known. Neither establishes the exact two-sided run-cap interface restrictions for every finite r>=2 or the full span-bivariate enumerator and geometric limit. The inspected primary papers focus on single-read constrained code size or on unrestricted two-read Type-A code design. Closest indexed exact graph and bounded-run-profile notes are distinguished by object and statistic. Priority is qualified because older non-indexed derivations might exist.
residual_risks: Priority risk: an older differently indexed analysis may already tabulate RLL-restricted two-read edge counts under another terminology.
A known single-read RLL source often means minimum zero-run length; the current maximum constant-run cap is a different constraint and cannot be conflated.
The published Type-A equivalence is a premise; this result makes no claim to a new proof of it.

value.rationale: Bounded maximum homopolymer lengths are natural channel-source constraints, and two-distinct-read reconstruction excludes precisely these induced-graph edges. The work supplies the complete all-alphabet, all-finite-r>=2, all-length graph edge invariant, refined by an intrinsically canonical disagreement span, plus a universal limiting geometric span law and an explicit average-degree coefficient. This quantifies conflict density and locality in a practically motivated constrained channel, beyond mere finite recomputation or the already known r=1 slice; it makes no unsupported optimum-code-size claim.
